method: Rows 1-15 of ~/codewatch-research/gaps/misses.tsv (the file was refreshed by the nightly run at 19:30 and none of its 182 rows had been noted before), in file order. All 182 rows are cve-pairs-php, so this batch is PHP only. For each case I read the fix commit (gh api repos/O/R/commits/SHA) and the advisory text from the local clone of the advisory database, then the files at the fix commit's parent where the diff did not show source or sink: YesWiki tools/bazar/templates/forms/forms_confirm.twig, tools/templates/templates/alert-message.twig and includes/services/TemplateEngine.php, includes/services/ThemeManager.php; Craft src/controllers/AssetsController.php and src/services/AssetTransforms.php (getTransformIndex/normalizeTransform); Pimcore models/DataObject/ClassDefinition/Data/ManyToManyRelation.php, models/DataObject/ClassDefinition/Service.php (importClassDefinitionFromJson) and models/DataObject/ClassDefinition/Helper/Dao.php; Froxlor lib/Froxlor/Api/Commands/SubDomains.php, Admins.php and IpsAndPorts.php; PureBlog includes/lib/content.php; AdminNeo admin/db.inc.php, admin/database.inc.php, admin/index.php and admin/include/bootstrap.inc.php; Contao core-bundle/src/Controller/ImagesController.php and core-bundle/src/Routing/ImagesLoader.php; phpMyFAQ phpmyfaq/assets/templates/admin/content/faq.editor.twig; Sulu src/Sulu/Bundle/MediaBundle/Controller/MediaStreamController.php; Snipe-IT app/Http/Requests/UploadFileRequest.php and app/Http/Controllers/Api/UploadedFilesController.php; Freeform packages/plugin/src/Library/Attributes/Attributes.php. Five cases are unsure for the reason written in their note: Craft (the fix only adds a type check; the RCE sink after normalizeTransform was not read), Pimcore's SQL injection (the admin grid filter reader that supplies $value was not read: models/DataObject/Listing/Dao.php does not hold it), AdminNeo's file deletion (the database-list page posting $_POST["db"] was not found among admin/*.inc.php; the advisory quotes it), Freeform (the submission reader that fills the attribute map was not read; the isolated Twig renderer and the excluded keys are in the diff), and Pimcore's field-name RCE (the admin import endpoint and the generated-class writer were not read; the setName() comment and the advisory describe them). No case was skipped. Rows 16-182 are left for the next run.

notes.sink: app/Http/Controllers/Api/UploadedFilesController.php:160-165 `if (request('inline') == 'true') { $headers = ['Content-Disposition' => 'inline']; return Storage::download(self::$map_storage_path[$object_type].$log->filename, $log->filename, $headers); }` - the attacker's file is served on the Snipe-IT origin with its own content type
notes.between: the uploaded file name is stored in the Actionlog and read back in show(); the API applies none of the safe-inline allowlist the web controller uses, so an XML document with an `xml-stylesheet` processing instruction is fetched as a document, the browser applies the attacker's XSLT and runs script in the victim's session (StorageHelper::downloader, used on the non-inline path, also lost the disposition)
notes.fix: adds a strict `allowed_inline_display` extension => MIME map in config/filesystems.php, cross-checks the server-detected MIME in StorageHelper::allowSafeInline(), serves inline only for an allowlisted extension+MIME (with nosniff), otherwise forces the attachment downloader, which now sends `application/octet-stream` + nosniff everywhere

ResponseHeaderBag::DISPOSITION_INLINE : ...; }` - the `?inline=1` query parameter on `/media/{id}/download/{slug}`, combined with an uploaded media file
notes.sink: src/Sulu/Bundle/MediaBundle/Controller/MediaStreamController.php:186-199 `$response->headers->set('Content-Type', !empty($mimeType) ? $mimeType : 'application/octet-stream'); $response->headers->set('Content-Disposition', $disposition);` - the stored file is returned inline with its stored MIME type and no CSP

notes.source: the `layoutDefinitions` JSON of an imported class definition: models/DataObject/ClassDefinition/Service.php:100-108 `$importData = json_decode($json, true); ... $layout = self::generateLayoutTreeFromArray($importData['layoutDefinitions'], ...)` - each field definition's `name`, set through `Data::setName()` (the admin import/save endpoint that posts this JSON was not read)
notes.sink: models/DataObject/ClassDefinition/Data.php:166-176 `setName()` stored the name verbatim; it is emitted into the generated PHP class (`protected $<name>;`) and into `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN`/`ADD INDEX` in models/DataObject/ClassDefinition/Helper/Dao.php:101-113, where the name was concatenated between backticks
notes.between: the imported field name is written into the class source Pimcore generates for the DataObject and into the DDL its Dao executes; a name such as `x;function __construct(){}//` closes the property declaration, so the injected PHP runs with the application's privileges, and a name with a backtick injects SQL into the ALTER TABLE statement
notes.fix: rejects any non-empty name not matching `/^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]{0,62}$/` in `setName()`, and quotes table/column/index names with `$db->quoteIdentifier()` in the Dao's ALTER TABLE statements
